question:
Which of the following pair regarding the Ruler of Delhi sultanate – period of their rule is correct?
I. Ghiyasuddin Balban – 1266-1287
II. Firuz Shah Tughluq – 1351-1388
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ghiyasuddin Balban ruled the Delhi Sultanate from 1266 to 1287 and was a powerful ruler of the Slave/Mamluk dynasty (गुलाम वंश), known for strengthening royal authority.

• Firuz Shah Tughluq ruled from 1351 to 1388 and belonged to the Tughlaq dynasty, so both pairings I and II are correct.

• Balban introduced the practices of Sijda (prostration) and Paibos (kissing the feet) to elevate the prestige of the throne.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Balban propounded the theory of kingship as the vice-regent of God (Niyabat-i-Khudai).

• Firuz Shah Tughluq is remembered for founding cities like Firozabad, Hisar, Jaunpur and building canals.

• Firuz Shah also imposed the Jizya as a separate tax and set up an employment bureau and a charity department.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): This would be true only if the second pair were wrong, but Firuz Shah Tughluq's dates (1351-1388) are also correct.

• Only II (Option 2): This would be true only if Balban's dates were wrong, but 1266-1287 for Balban is correct.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, since both the pairings are historically accurate.

question: Which article of the Indian constitution is related with Power of Parliament to amend the Constitution and procedure therefor?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 368.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 368 of Part XX deals with the Power of Parliament to amend the Constitution and the procedure therefor (संविधान संशोधन की प्रक्रिया).

• It provides for two special majority procedures and, for certain provisions, ratification by half of the state legislatures.

• The basic structure of the Constitution cannot be amended under Article 368, as held in the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Constitution can be amended by a simple majority, special majority, or special majority with state ratification.

• The 24th Amendment Act, 1971 made it obligatory for the President to give assent to a Constitutional Amendment Bill.

• Article 368 falls under Part XX of the Constitution.

NOTE

• Article 355 (Option 1): Duty of the Union to protect states against external aggression and internal disturbance.

• Article 375 (Option 3): Courts, authorities and officers to continue to function subject to the provisions of the Constitution.

• Article 394 (Option 4): Deals with the commencement of certain articles of the Constitution.

question: Article 126 of the Indian Constitution mentions _____.
option_2: Appointment of acting Chief Justice of India
option_3: Supreme Court to be a court of record
solution_text:
The correct answer is Appointment of acting Chief Justice of India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 126 provides for the appointment of an acting Chief Justice of India (कार्यवाहक मुख्य न्यायाधीश की नियुक्ति) by the President when the office is vacant or the CJI is unable to perform duties.

• The acting CJI is appointed from among the other Judges of the Supreme Court.

• It ensures continuity in the functioning of the highest judiciary.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Articles 124 to 147 in Part V deal with the Supreme Court of India.

• The Supreme Court was established on 28 January 1950.

• The CJI is appointed by the President under Article 124.

NOTE

• Appointment of ad hoc Judges (Option 1): This is provided under Article 127 of the Constitution.

• Supreme Court to be a court of record (Option 3): This is dealt with under Article 129.

• Seat of Supreme Court (Option 4): This is provided under Article 130.

question: The New Development Bank is associated with which of the following international organisation?
solution_text:
The correct answer is BRICS.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The New Development Bank (NDB) was established by the BRICS (ब्रिक्स) nations in 2014 and became operational in 2015.

• Its headquarters is in Shanghai, China.

• The NDB was set up to mobilise resources for infrastructure and sustainable development projects in BRICS and other emerging economies.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• BRICS originally consisted of Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa.

• The first President of the NDB was K. V. Kamath of India.

• The idea of the NDB was proposed at the 4th BRICS Summit in New Delhi (2012).

NOTE

• World Trade Organisation (Option 2): A global body regulating international trade, headquartered in Geneva.

• QUAD (Option 3): A strategic security dialogue among India, USA, Japan and Australia.

• SAARC (Option 4): South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation, headquartered in Kathmandu, Nepal.

question: Where was the BIMSTEC Summit held in April 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Thailand.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 6th BIMSTEC Summit was held in Bangkok, Thailand (थाईलैंड) on 4 April 2025.

• Thailand held the chairmanship of BIMSTEC for this summit.

• Prime Minister Narendra Modi attended the summit representing India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• BIMSTEC stands for the Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation.

• It has seven member states: Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand.

• The BIMSTEC Secretariat is located in Dhaka, Bangladesh.

NOTE

• India (Option 1): India is a founding member of BIMSTEC but did not host the April 2025 summit.

• Bangladesh (Option 2): Hosts the BIMSTEC Secretariat but did not host the 6th summit.

• Bhutan (Option 3): A member state, but not the venue of the April 2025 summit.

question: Amitabh Bachchan had been selected for the Dada Saheb Phalke award for the year _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2018.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Legendary actor Amitabh Bachchan was selected for the Dada Saheb Phalke Award (दादा साहेब फाल्के पुरस्कार) for the year 2018.

• The award was presented to him in 2019.

• It is the highest award in the field of Indian cinema.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Dada Saheb Phalke Award was instituted in 1969.

• The first recipient of the award was actress Devika Rani.

• It is conferred by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.

NOTE

• 2014 (Option 1): The Dada Saheb Phalke Award for 2014 was given to actor Shashi Kapoor.

• 2016 (Option 2): The award for 2016 was conferred on actor Vinod Khanna (posthumously).

• 2020 (Option 4): The award for 2020 was given to actress Asha Parekh.

question: Who among the following was the first Indian female doctor of western medicine?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Anandibai Gopalrao Joshi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Anandibai Gopalrao Joshi is regarded as the first Indian female doctor of western medicine (पश्चिमी चिकित्सा की पहली भारतीय महिला डॉक्टर).

• She earned her degree in medicine from the Woman's Medical College of Pennsylvania, USA in 1886.

• She was among the earliest Indian women to study and qualify in Western medicine abroad.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Anandibai Joshi was born on 31 March 1865 in Kalyan, Maharashtra.

• She was encouraged in her studies by her husband, Gopalrao Joshi.

• She died young in 1887 at the age of 22.

NOTE

• EK Janaki Ammal (Option 1): A renowned Indian botanist known for her work on sugarcane and plant cytogenetics.

• Rupa Bai Furdoonji (Option 2): Regarded as one of the world's first women anaesthetists.

• Mary Poonen Lukose (Option 3): The first Indian woman to become a Surgeon General and a pioneering gynaecologist.

question: Who has been appointed as the President of the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) for FY 2025-26?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajiv Memani.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rajiv Memani was appointed as the President of the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) for FY 2025-26 (भारतीय उद्योग परिसंघ का अध्यक्ष).

• He is the Chairman and CEO of EY India.

• He took over from Sanjiv Puri, the outgoing CII President.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• CII is a non-government, industry-led and industry-managed organisation founded in 1895.

• Its headquarters is in New Delhi.

• CII works to create and sustain an environment conducive to the development of industry in India.

NOTE

• Sanjiv Puri (Option 1): Chairman of ITC and the CII President for the previous term (FY 2024-25).

• R Mukundan (Option 2): Managing Director of Tata Chemicals and a CII President-designate/Vice President.

• T Rabi Sankar (Option 4): A Deputy Governor of the Reserve Bank of India.

question: In July 2024, Om Prakash Mathur has been appointed as Governor of _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sikkim.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In July 2024, Om Prakash Mathur was appointed as the Governor of Sikkim (सिक्किम का राज्यपाल).

• He was sworn in as the 18th Governor of Sikkim on 31 July 2024.

• The Governor is the constitutional head of a state, appointed by the President.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Sikkim became the 22nd state of India in 1975.

• The capital of Sikkim is Gangtok.

• The Governor of a state is appointed under Article 155 of the Constitution.

NOTE

• Assam (Option 1): Its Governor is a separate appointment; Om Prakash Mathur was made Governor of Sikkim.

• Tripura (Option 3): A north-eastern state with its own separately appointed Governor.

• Nagaland (Option 4): A north-eastern state with a separately appointed Governor.

question: In June 2025, EPFO's revised his auto-settlement limit. This limit is now Rs. _____ lakh.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 5.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In June 2025, the EPFO raised its auto-settlement of advance limit to Rs. 5 lakh (पाँच लाख रुपये की ऑटो-सेटलमेंट सीमा).

• Earlier this auto-settlement limit was Rs. 1 lakh.

• The move was aimed at faster and more efficient settlement of advance claims.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• EPFO stands for the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation.

• It functions under the Ministry of Labour and Employment.

• The Auto-settlement facility settles eligible claims automatically without manual intervention.

NOTE

• 1 (Option 1): Rs. 1 lakh was the earlier auto-settlement limit before the June 2025 revision.

• 2 (Option 2): Not the revised limit set by EPFO in June 2025.

• 10 (Option 4): Not the auto-settlement limit; the revised limit is Rs. 5 lakh.

question: Which ministry oversees Pradhan Mantri Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana Launched in February 2024?
option_3: Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of New & Renewable Energy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Pradhan Mantri Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, launched in February 2024, is overseen by the Ministry of New & Renewable Energy (नवीन एवं नवीकरणीय ऊर्जा मंत्रालय).

• The scheme aims to provide free electricity to households through rooftop solar installations.

• It targets about one crore households under the rooftop solar programme.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The scheme provides subsidies for installing rooftop solar panels.

• It was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

• India aims to boost solar energy capacity as part of its renewable energy goals.

NOTE

• Ministry of Power (Option 1): Handles electricity generation, transmission and distribution policy, but not this specific rooftop solar scheme.

• Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change (Option 3): Deals with environmental protection and climate policy.

• Ministry of Rural Development (Option 4): Focuses on rural welfare and development schemes.

question: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas has on 4 August 2025 issued a detailed response to certain concerns raised on the impact of _____ percent Ethanol Blended Petrol on mileage and vehicle life.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 20.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• On 4 August 2025, the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas addressed concerns on 20 percent Ethanol Blended Petrol (E20) (बीस प्रतिशत इथेनॉल मिश्रित पेट्रोल) and its impact on mileage and vehicle life.

• E20 refers to petrol blended with 20% ethanol.

• India achieved the 20% ethanol blending target ahead of the original 2030 schedule.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme aims to reduce import dependence and cut emissions.

• Ethanol blending helps save foreign exchange and supports farmers.

• The programme is part of India's push towards biofuels and energy security.

NOTE

• 40 (Option 2): Not the current blending level being discussed; India's target is 20% ethanol.

• 60 (Option 3): Not a petrol ethanol-blending percentage used in India.

• 50 (Option 4): Not the ethanol blend level referenced in the ministry's response.

question: _____ was the first Indian to win a medal in Birmingham Commonwealth Games 2022.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sanket Sargar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sanket Sargar was the first Indian to win a medal at the Birmingham Commonwealth Games 2022 (बर्मिंघम राष्ट्रमंडल खेल 2022).

• He won a silver medal in weightlifting in the men's 55 kg category.

• This was India's opening medal of the 2022 CWG.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Birmingham Commonwealth Games 2022 were held in England.

• India finished fourth in the overall medal tally at these Games.

• Weightlifting gave India several early medals at the event.

NOTE

• Mirabai Chanu (Option 2): Won a gold medal in weightlifting (49 kg) at the same Games, but not India's first medal.

• Harjinder Kaur (Option 3): Won a bronze medal in weightlifting at the 2022 CWG.

• Vikas Thakur (Option 4): Won a silver medal in weightlifting at the 2022 CWG.

question: Which of the following sport was not played in the Summer Olympics 2024?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ice Skating.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ice Skating (आइस स्केटिंग) was not played in the Summer Olympics 2024 as it is a Winter Olympic sport.

• The Paris 2024 Summer Olympics featured summer sports like badminton, tennis and basketball.

• Ice skating events are held at the Winter Olympic Games.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The 2024 Summer Olympics were held in Paris, France.

• New sports at Paris 2024 included breaking (breakdancing).

• India won a total of six medals at the Paris 2024 Olympics.

NOTE

• Badminton (Option 2): A regular event at the Summer Olympics, including Paris 2024.

• Lawn tennis (Option 3): Tennis is a well-established Summer Olympic sport.

• Basketball (Option 4): Both men's and women's basketball are part of the Summer Olympics.

question: Which of the following institution has developed a device named "AroTrack"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is IIT Bombay.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• IIT Bombay developed the device named "AroTrack" (एरोट्रैक).

• AroTrack is a portable device used to detect water pollutants, particularly aromatic compounds like phenol and benzene.

• It works even in remote areas without a power source, making water quality testing quick and easy.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs) are premier engineering and research institutions.

• IIT Bombay was established in 1958.

• Such biosensor-based devices support environmental monitoring initiatives.

NOTE

• IISC Bangalore (Option 2): India's premier research institute, but not the developer of AroTrack.

• IIT Kanpur (Option 3): A leading IIT, but not associated with this particular device.

• IIT Roorkee (Option 4): One of the oldest IITs, but not the developer of AroTrack.

question: The Aravalli Green Wall Project is a major initiative to spread green cover in the _____ km buffer area around the Aravalli hill range.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 5.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Aravalli Green Wall Project aims to spread green cover in a 5 km buffer area (पाँच किलोमीटर बफर क्षेत्र) around the Aravalli hill range.

• It is part of a larger initiative to combat land degradation and desertification.

• The project covers the states of Haryana, Rajasthan, Gujarat and Delhi.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Aravalli range is one of the oldest fold mountain ranges in the world.

• The project aligns with India's target to restore degraded land and create carbon sinks.

• It is inspired by the concept of Africa's Great Green Wall.

NOTE

• 35 (Option 2): Not the buffer distance specified for the Aravalli Green Wall Project.

• 60 (Option 3): Not the correct buffer area width for the project.

• 125 (Option 4): Not the buffer distance; the project targets a 5 km buffer zone.

question: Who among the following invented the game of judo?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jigoro Kano.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Jigoro Kano of Japan is credited with inventing the game of Judo (जूडो) in 1882.

• Judo is a martial art and combat sport that developed from jujutsu.

• Kano founded the Kodokan institute to teach and promote judo.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Judo became an Olympic sport for men at the 1964 Tokyo Olympics.

• The term Judo means the gentle way.

• Jigoro Kano is also known as the father of Japanese sports.

NOTE

• James Naismith (Option 2): Invented the game of basketball in 1891.

• James Creighton (Option 3): Credited with organising the first indoor game of ice hockey.

• Ebenezer Morley (Option 4): Known as the father of the Football Association and modern football.

question: In January 2025, India Open badminton tournament was held in _____
solution_text:
The correct answer is New Delhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In January 2025, the India Open badminton tournament was held in New Delhi (नई दिल्ली).

• The tournament is a BWF World Tour Super 750 event.

• It is one of the premier badminton events hosted by India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The India Open is organised by the Badminton Association of India (BAI).

• The event is usually held at the K. D. Jadhav Indoor Hall, New Delhi.

• It attracts top international badminton players.

NOTE

• Chennai (Option 2): Capital of Tamil Nadu, but not the venue of the January 2025 India Open.

• Bengaluru (Option 3): Capital of Karnataka, not the host city of this tournament.

• Kolkata (Option 4): Capital of West Bengal, not the venue of the India Open 2025.

question: Which festival of Kerala has entered the Guinness World Records for being the single largest gathering of women for a religious activity?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Attukal Pongala.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Attukal Pongala (अट्टुकल पोंगल) of Kerala entered the Guinness World Records for being the single largest gathering of women for a religious activity.

• It is celebrated at the Attukal Bhagavathy Temple in Thiruvananthapuram.

• Women gather in large numbers to prepare Pongala (a sweet offering) as a devotional ritual.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Attukal Bhagavathy Temple is often called the 'Sabarimala of Women'.

• The festival is spread over several days in the Malayalam month of Makaram-Kumbham.

• It is a major religious event drawing devotees from across India.

NOTE

• Chikalkalo (Option 1): A festival, but not the one that holds this Guinness World Record.

• Pooram (Option 2): A famous temple festival of Kerala (e.g., Thrissur Pooram) known for elephants and fireworks.

• Vishu (Option 3): The Malayalam New Year festival celebrated in Kerala.

question: Around which year was Robert Clive appointed the Governor of Bengal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1764.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Robert Clive was appointed the Governor of Bengal (बंगाल का गवर्नर) around 1764-1765, taking up his second term.

• He established the Dual System of Government in Bengal in 1765.

• Under this system the Company controlled revenue (Diwani) while the Nawab held nominal administration.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Robert Clive won the Battle of Plassey in 1757 and the Battle of Buxar in 1764.

• He secured the Diwani rights of Bengal, Bihar and Odisha through the Treaty of Allahabad (1765).

• He is often regarded as the founder of British political power in India.

NOTE

• 1733 (Option 1): Robert Clive was born in 1725, so he could not have been Governor in 1733.

• 1752 (Option 2): Clive was still an early Company official/soldier at this time, not the Governor of Bengal.

• 1781 (Option 4): By this year Clive had already died (1774); it does not mark his governorship.

question: In which year did the committee for reforms in the insurance sector formed under the chairmanship of R.N. Malhotra submitted its report?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1994.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The committee for reforms in the insurance sector under R.N. Malhotra submitted its report in 1994 (मल्होत्रा समिति की रिपोर्ट).

• The Malhotra Committee was set up in 1993 to examine the structure of the insurance industry.

• It recommended opening up the insurance sector to private players.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• R.N. Malhotra was a former Governor of the Reserve Bank of India.

• The committee's recommendations led to the creation of the IRDA (Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority).

• The IRDA Act was passed in 1999.

NOTE

• 1991 (Option 1): The year of major economic reforms/LPG, but not when the Malhotra Committee reported.

• 1992 (Option 2): Not the year the insurance reforms committee submitted its report.

• 1995 (Option 4): Close but incorrect; the report was submitted in 1994.

question: The _____ took place in Assam in 1906.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Revolt of Songram Sangma.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Revolt of Songram Sangma (सोंग्राम संगमा का विद्रोह) took place in Assam in 1906.

• It was a tribal uprising of the Garo people against British rule.

• The revolt was triggered largely by new British forest laws restricting the tribals' traditional rights.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Songram Sangma led the Garos of the Garo Hills region against British authority.

• Tribal revolts were a significant part of India's resistance to colonial rule.

• The British forest policies declared forests as state property, angering tribal communities.

NOTE

• Self Respect Movement (Option 2): A social movement started by E. V. Ramasamy (Periyar) in Tamil Nadu in the 1920s.

• Blue rebellion (Option 3): The Indigo Revolt (Nil Vidroh) of Bengal in 1859-60 by indigo cultivators.

• Koli Revolt (Option 4): An uprising by the Koli community in western India during the 19th century.

question: The gross fiscal deficit as a ratio to GDP in India had climbed to _____ per cent by 1990-91.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 10.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• By 1990-91, the gross fiscal deficit as a ratio to GDP (सकल राजकोषीय घाटा) in India had climbed to about 10 per cent.

• This high fiscal deficit was a key feature of the economic crisis of 1991.

• The crisis eventually led to the introduction of economic reforms (LPG) in 1991.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The 1991 crisis was marked by a severe balance of payments problem and low foreign exchange reserves.

• India had to pledge gold and approach the IMF for a loan.

• The reforms of 1991 introduced Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation (LPG).

NOTE

• 25 (Option 2): Far too high; the gross fiscal deficit to GDP was around 10 per cent, not 25.

• 30 (Option 3): Not the correct figure for the fiscal deficit ratio in 1990-91.

• 45 (Option 4): An unrealistically high value; the correct figure is about 10 per cent.

question: What subject does Article 77 of the Indian Constitution pertain to?
option_3: Conduct of business of the Government of India
option_4: Council of Ministers to aid and advise President
solution_text:
The correct answer is Conduct of business of the Government of India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 77 deals with the Conduct of business of the Government of India (भारत सरकार के कार्य का संचालन).

• It states that all executive actions of the Government of India shall be expressed to be taken in the name of the President.

• It also empowers the President to make rules for the more convenient transaction of government business.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Articles 74 and 75 deal with the Council of Ministers and the Prime Minister.

• Article 78 deals with the duties of the Prime Minister regarding furnishing of information to the President.

• Part V of the Constitution deals with the Union executive.

NOTE

• Rights of ministers in Parliament (Option 1): Related to Article 88, which allows ministers to speak in either House.

• Duties of prime minister (Option 2): These are dealt with under Article 78, not Article 77.

• Council of Ministers to aid and advise President (Option 4): This is provided under Article 74.

question: Members of the Legislative Council of an Indian state as nearly as may be, _____ shall be elected by electorates consisting of members of municipalities, district boards and such other local authorities in the State as Parliament may by law specify.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1/3.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per Article 171, nearly one-third (1/3) (एक-तिहाई) of the members of a State Legislative Council are elected by local authorities like municipalities and district boards.

• The Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) is the upper house of a state legislature.

• Its composition is governed by Article 171 of the Constitution.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• About 1/3 are elected by members of the state legislative assembly.

• About 1/12 are elected by graduates and another 1/12 by teachers.

• The remaining 1/6 members are nominated by the Governor.

NOTE

• 1/12 (Option 1): This fraction applies to members elected by graduates and by teachers separately, not by local authorities.

• 1/2 (Option 3): No category of the Legislative Council is filled by exactly one-half of the members.

• 1/6 (Option 4): This is the fraction of members nominated by the Governor, not elected by local bodies.
